Hi Natalie — looping in our procurement and marketplace ops leads so we can get you the precise checklist. See initial guidance below and we'll follow up with the intake packet.

High-level:
- Required intake: vendor intake form (company details, tax ID, banking), signed MSA (DocuSign), up-to-date SOC2 report (if available), W-9/W-8 as applicable, and a corporate entity verification (Articles of Org / Certificate of Incorporation).
- Marketplace-specific PO routing: AWS and Azure accept POs routed to our central finance inbox (invoices@redwood.ai) with a vendor code; GCP typically uses managed billing through the marketplace channel which needs a separate vendor ID and bank/payment setup.
- Settlement terms: net 30 typical for direct contracts; marketplace settlements follow the marketplace payout schedule (can be delayed by their disbursement cadence). We can provide sample invoice templates for each marketplace.

Next steps: Vanessa, Marcus — can you attach the vendor intake packet and the latest MSA draft? Marcus, please note StellarData will likely list on all three clouds and may ask about holdbacks/escrow.

Natalie — if you can send over your legal billing entity name and tax ID, we can pre-fill the intake form before the call.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Hi Natalie — attaching the vendor intake packet and our current MSA (v2) for your legal team to review. I included a short checklist below that maps required docs to each marketplace.

Attachments: vendor_intake_form.pdf (application/pdf), redwood_msa_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), SOC2_summary.pdf (application/pdf)

Checklist (quick):
- All marketplaces: completed vendor_intake_form.pdf, signed MSA (DocuSign link below), W-9 (US entities) or W-8BEN-E (non-US), company incorporation docs, bank details for payouts.
- AWS: vendor code + finance inbox -> invoices@redwood.ai; PO should reference Redwood vendor code RDWD-AWS-XXXX. AWS settlements are on their payout schedule (monthly, with ~30-45 day lag).
- Azure: we support Marketplace ISV procurement flow (PO to invoices@redwood.ai) but Azure requires an additional Marketplace Contract ID.
- GCP: uses Managed Marketplace billing — we need bank onboarding + vendor ID; payouts come via Google with their cadence and fees.

Procurement exceptions and holdbacks:
- Some enterprise buyers ask us to accept a PO with a short-term holdback clause for first 90 days (common for new sellers). We typically accept limited holdbacks if accompanied by standard warranty language in the SOW. Full escrow is rare on marketplace listings — that is usually between seller and marketplace.

Natalie — quick answers ahead of the call:

1) PO retention/holdback: We can accept limited retention clauses for direct enterprise POs if the clause is narrowly scoped (e.g., 10% retention for 60 days tied to delivery milestones). Any language that goes beyond standard warranty/indemnity will need legal review and may require redlines to the MSA. We'll flag those on the call and route to Legal if needed.

2) GCP disputes/chargebacks: Marketplace chargebacks and refunds are handled through GCP; Redwood will assist in resolving disputes that impact payouts to the seller (we act as the marketplace partner), but StellarData should be prepared to provide evidence and cooperate on merchant disputes.

Agenda for Thu 10am PT:
- Intake form walkthrough (Vanessa)
- MSA and PO redline expectations (Jordan + Legal overview)
- Marketplace-specific billing & payout timelines (Marcus)

Call invite sent; joining info is in the HubSpot record. If anything changes, ping me. Looking forward to getting StellarData live.
